newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's slow growth holding inflation in check.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's slow growth holding inflation in check.

text.p: Slower than expected economic growth is helping hold back Venezuelan inflation, which fell to 1.8 percent in June from 3.1 percent in May, Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said.
Market estimates had hovered around 2.6 percent for June.

Casas told reporters the good result was due to "a more rational fiscal policy, effective Central Bank open market operations and evidently demand that has not re-activated as expected due to the slow-growing economy."
Government ministers have forecast over five percent growth for this year and the next after the economy shrank nearly two percent in 1996.

Casas added Venezuela was now on track to hit its 30 percent year-end inflation target. With cumulative January to June inflation now at 14.6 percent, versus 62.3 percent over the same period last year, "Anyone who thinks we can't make 30 percent inflation for this year is wrong," Casas said.
